- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; increase forecast slightly to account for potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–5 days; apply downward bias to subsequent forecasts.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; check for lagged sentiment influence and adjust forecast mid-horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates near-term (first 7–10 days) if sentiment is positive; apply downward correction for early horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or negative values, model tends to underperform; increase forecast baseline by 1–2% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
